mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 months reduces discount rates applied to future equity cash flows, increasing the present value of expected returns and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% in a single month signals tightening monetary policy, raising discount rates and compressing expected equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs for 3 consecutive months indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in strengthening periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below -50,000 jobs for 3 consecutive months signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer and business confidence and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
